title: Macroeconomics
completion_message: ¡Formidable! Ahora dominas el vocabulario de las altas finanzas globales. Hablar de inflación, tasas de interés, aranceles y el PIB te permite analizar el entorno macroeconómico como un verdadero experto.

parts.visual:
Para entender el mundo empresarial a nivel macro, necesitas dominar estos términos financieros: 

1. Inflation (Inflación): 
- El aumento general de los precios y la caída del poder adquisitivo del dinero. 
Ej: High INFLATION is destroying the consumers' purchasing power. 

2. Interest rates (Tasas de interés): 
- El costo de pedir dinero prestado, fijado por los bancos centrales. 
Ej: The central bank raised INTEREST RATES to combat inflation. 

3. GDP / Gross Domestic Product (PIB / Producto Interno Bruto): 
- El valor total de todos los bienes y servicios producidos en un país. 
Ej: The country's GDP grew by 3% last year.
parts.audio: Welcome to Macroeconomics and Global Markets. To understand the business world at a macro level, you need to master these financial terms. Number 1: Inflation. This is the general increase in prices and the fall in the purchasing power of money. For example: High INFLATION is destroying the consumers' purchasing power. Number 2: Interest rates. This is the cost of borrowing money, usually set by central banks. For example: The central bank raised INTEREST RATES to combat inflation. Number 3: GDP, which stands for Gross Domestic Product. This represents the total value of all goods and services produced within a country. For example: The country's GDP grew by 3% last year.

parts.visual:
4. Protectionism (Proteccionismo): 
- Política económica de restringir las importaciones para proteger las industrias locales. 
Ej: The new government's trade policy relies heavily on PROTECTIONISM. 

5. Tariffs (Aranceles): 
- Impuestos a los bienes importados o exportados. 
Ej: They imposed high TARIFFS on imported steel. 

6. Supply chain (Cadena de suministro): 
- Toda la red de personas y empresas involucradas en la creación y distribución de un producto. 
Ej: The pandemic severely disrupted global SUPPLY CHAINS. 

7. Bull vs. Bear market (Mercado alcista vs. bajista): 
- Bull = los precios suben. Bear = los precios bajan. 
Ej: Investors are making a lot of money in this BULL market.
parts.audio: Number 4: Protectionism. The economic policy of restricting imports from other countries to protect domestic industries. For example: The new government's trade policy relies heavily on PROTECTIONISM. Number 5: Tariffs. Taxes imposed on imported or exported goods. For example: They imposed high TARIFFS on imported steel. Number 6: Supply chain. The entire network of individuals, organizations, resources, and technologies involved in creating and selling a product. For example: The pandemic severely disrupted global SUPPLY CHAINS. Number 7: Bull versus Bear market. A Bull market means stock prices are rising. A Bear market means prices are falling. For example: Investors are making a lot of money in this BULL market.

questions.question: Due to high ____, the cost of living has doubled in the last five years, but salaries haven't changed.
The central bank decided to lower interest ____ to encourage people to take loans and buy houses.
China has the second largest ____ (Gross Domestic Product) in the world. (PIB).
questions.explanation: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) = PIB (Producto Interno Bruto).

questions.question: To protect local farmers, the government imposed heavy ____ on imported agricultural products. (Aranceles).
The global ____ chain was severely disrupted when the Suez Canal was blocked. (Cadena de suministro).
A period of economic decline where the GDP falls for two consecutive quarters is officially called a ____.
questions.explanation: Recession = recesión (2 trimestres de caída del PIB).

questions.question: When the stock market is rising and investors are optimistic, it is known as a ____ market.
When the stock market is falling and investors are pessimistic, it is known as a ____ market.
An economic policy that restricts international trade to help domestic industries is called ____.
If a country imports more goods than it exports, it has a trade ____. (Déficit comercial).
If a country exports more goods than it imports, it has a trade ____. (Superávit comercial).
The total amount of money that a government owes to its creditors is the national ____. (Deuda nacional).
When a currency loses value compared to other currencies, it is called ____. (Devaluación/Depreciación).
questions.explanation: Depreciation (o devaluation) = depreciación de la moneda.

questions.question: The ____ rate is the percentage of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work. (Tasa de desempleo).
A tax levied on a specific product, like alcohol or tobacco, is called an ____ tax.
questions.explanation: Excise tax = impuesto al consumo específico (alcohol, tabaco, gasolina).

questions.question: The ____ power of the dollar has decreased significantly over the last 50 years. (Poder adquisitivo).
When prices drop because there is too much supply and not enough demand, it is called ____.
A situation where an economy experiences stagnant growth and high inflation at the same time is called ____.
Money given by the government to a private business to keep the price of a product low is called a ____. (Subsidio).
The process of moving a company's production back to its home country from overseas is called ____.
questions.explanation: Reshoring (o onshoring) = relocalización de la producción al país de origen.

questions.question: High ____ is raising prices. (Inflación con I)
Interest ____. (Tasas de interés con R)
The country's ____. (PIB con G)
Import ____. (Aranceles con T)
The ____ chain. (Cadena de suministro con S)
A ____ market. (Mercado alcista con B)
A ____ market. (Mercado bajista con B)
Trade ____. (Déficit comercial con D)
Trade ____. (Superávit comercial con S)
Economic ____. (Recesión con R)
